title: vLLM Harmony tool continuation drops cache salt
summary: In GPT-OSS Harmony tool workflows on POST /v1/responses, the first engine request includes the caller’s cache_salt but the tool-continuation request rebuilds engine input without it. The continuation prefix enters the shared unsalted cache. Under the advisory’s conditions, another authenticated tenant can use a guessable post-tool prefix and exact cached-token counts to infer whether that prefix was processed; this is a membership oracle, not exposure of arbitrary prompt contents.
ai_role: The vLLM project advisory explicitly states that this vulnerability was discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber as part of the Patch the Planet security initiative. This establishes AI-enabled discovery attribution; the source does not establish model autonomy or the private discovery date.
classification_note: The project advisory was published on 2026-09-28 and describes a proposed fix. It does not establish whether the issue was known to defenders or exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The advisory lists versions below 0.30.0 as affected and versions 0.30.0 and later as patched; it also links the proposed fix PR #51818. The earliest affected version is unresolved in the advisory, and patch deployment is not inferred.

impacts.conditions: Requires a shared vLLM deployment with a GPT-OSS Harmony model on /v1/responses, prefix caching enabled, an operator-enabled built-in or MCP tool, a victim request that sets cache_salt and completes a tool continuation, and an authenticated attacker able to reconstruct the post-tool token prefix.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a proof-of-concept membership oracle; it does not report observed exploitation or arbitrary prompt-content disclosure.
